_comment: Run hmp9 — BL-125, a DOCS-ONLY correction to design/archive/bl124-s2-deploy.md §5, which claims the non-reply sink writes a {kind:boot} line at every boot. It does not: the marker is emitted inside NonReplySink's private write(), behind bootPending, and write() is reached only by a notice — apps/orchestrator/src/server.ts states the intent at the wiring site ('Nothing is opened until a notice actually arrives'). Brief: design/operator/hmp9-brief.md — modeled on hmp7 (a doing run), NOT on meta-brief.md, which instantiates brief-AUTHORING rungs only; the recursion fence was run against it (findsLaunchInstruction → null) rather than eyeballed. Bar: design/operator/hmp9-bar.md — R2 is the deciding row and is weighted heaviest: the target paragraph is HALF TRUE, and the per-boot reduction rule it also states is load-bearing for S3, so a delivery that fixes the false claim by deleting the paragraph FAILS even though the false sentence is gone. R3 (correct the false half) × R2 (keep the true half) were checked for mutual satisfiability in writing — they constrain different sentences, and a bar phrased 'rewrite §5' × 'do not change §5' would have been unsatisfiable while looking reasonable. AGENTTALK_NON_REPLY_SINK_PATH IS CONTAINMENT, NOT CONFIGURATION: the sink's default path resolves off os.homedir() and is therefore machine-global, not per-instance, so this backend on port 3600 would otherwise append its own notices into the LIVE BL-124 measurement at ~/.agenttalk/agent-non-reply.jsonl — indistinguishable from real traffic. That hazard did not exist before 2026-08-13 21:07, when S1 was deployed to the live orchestrator (pid 672 → 89437); it is the first operator run for which it does. The S1 closure had already redirected the test suite for exactly this reason and nobody had yet extended the reasoning to an operator-launched instance. CAP: cap.meter does NOT terminate anything (BL-117, 2026-08-06) — mandatory to configure, the commission refuses missing-cap-meter, but it fires on machine-wide per-provider totals and cannot separate this worker's spend from the supervising session's; on hmp5 it killed complete, verified work fourteen seconds after the commit. cap.wallClockMs is the ONLY rail that stops a run and since BL-118 its termination cascades to the provider CLI. Set deliberately, NOT copied: 2400000 ms (40 min), against hmp7's 90 (engine code) and hmp8's 60 (~150 lines of prose) — this run reads one document, one backlog item and three symbols, then rewrites one paragraph. AGENTTALK_WORKER_TURN_TIMEOUT_MS is likewise deliberate at 900000 (15 min) rather than the 1800000 both prior runs used: with a 40-minute rail, a 30-minute turn timeout would let a single wedged turn consume most of the run before the only real rail fired. instance.orchestratorUrl is REQUIRED even with a startCommand: the client's start script takes it from THIS config and only parses mcpUrl from the backend's stdout — omitting it fails with 'createLauncherCore requires orchestratorUrl', which is what killed hmp1's first attempt. startCommand.cwd is the ORCHESTRATOR (AgentTalk's backend); the WORKER's workdir is a separate AgentTalk worktree. Paths are macOS, where os.tmpdir() is /var/folders/… — so the sandbox must be created with an explicit root of /tmp to match the workdir below, exactly as hmp7 and hmp8 did. PRE-FLIGHT, NOT YET DONE at the time of writing: /tmp/att-op-hmp9 does not exist, and design/operator/hmp9.authorized does not exist and is the PO's to write. The commission refuses workdir-missing until the worktree is provisioned, and governance-missing unless it contains CLAUDE.md — provisioning is the operator's job (runbook §1), deliberately not the verifier's. repo-sha at the time of writing is 99626b0f22d57e2e4466366e66c46f518a214fa1; if anything lands on master before this run, it must be re-pinned — that is the sha-moved refusal, and it exists so the PO never authorizes work they did not see.
goal: Implement backlog item BL-125, following design/operator/hmp9-brief.md in your workdir: correct the false claim in design/archive/bl124-s2-deploy.md §5 that the non-reply sink writes a boot line at every boot, while PRESERVING the true half of the same paragraph — the per-boot reduction rule. Change exactly one file and commit it on your branch. If you conclude the code is wrong rather than the document, stop and report with evidence; that is a success.
